summary: Today’s pulse tracks Nineteen people taken to hospital after England fire, as thousands evacuated in Croatia – Europe live, UK a ‘tinderbox’, says Burnham, as he calls in military and bans disposable barbecues – UK politics live, and Italian police recover paintings by Cézanne, Renoir and Matisse after heist. Across Guardian, the strongest repeated signals are record, burnham, and court. In the background, Luigi Mangione to appear in court amid reports of plea deal over healthcare CEO’s killing – live and Andy Burnham moves to cut new EV sales targets keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Nineteen people taken to hospital after England fire, as thousands evacuated in Croatia – Europe live
headlines.description: A total of 54 people were treated by paramedics after West Midlands fire as blazes continue across Europe amid extreme heat People taken to hospital and homes damaged in West Midlands fires England has received just 4mm of rain so far in August, or 6% of the long-term average for the month , the Environment Agency said on Friday, as reported by PA. It follows the driest July on record for the country , when only 7mm of rain was measured, or 10% of the average.

headlines.title: UK a ‘tinderbox’, says Burnham, as he calls in military and bans disposable barbecues – UK politics live
headlines.description: PM also says fire and rescue services will be given more cash This election is a novelty with a record 34 candidates, including Howling Laud Hope of The Official Monster Raving Loony Party and Marcus White from the Everyone is God Party. They have pounded the streets of Clacton over the past few weeks as they seek to win the support of about 80,000 voters.

headlines.title: Italian police recover paintings by Cézanne, Renoir and Matisse after heist
headlines.description: Artworks valued at total of more than $10m were stolen from Magnani Rocca Foundation near Parma in March Italian police have recovered three paintings by the French masters Paul Cézanne, Pierre-Auguste Renoir and Henri Matisse that were stolen earlier this year from a private museum near the northern city of Parma, authorities have said. The raid took place overnight on 22-23 March at the Magnani Rocca Foundation, about 12 miles (19km) from Parma, after a series of high-profile thefts from other European museums.

headlines.title: Luigi Mangione to appear in court amid reports of plea deal over healthcare CEO’s killing – live
headlines.description: Earlier this week prosecutors and Luigi Mangione’s lawyers filed a joint letter requesting the hearing at 11am on Friday in Manhattan federal court Good morning from Manhattan federal court! Luigi Mangione is expected to appear at 11am ET after a hastily scheduled conference that has spurred intense speculation that he might plead guilty related to the killing of UnitedHealthcare executive Brian Thompson.

headlines.title: Andy Burnham moves to cut new EV sales targets
headlines.description: Possible cut from 80% down to as little as 50% could add millions of tonnes of CO2 to emissions and comes amid UK heatwaves Andy Burnham’s government has said it will look at cutting electric vehicle sales targets, in proposals that could add millions of tonnes a year to the UK’s future carbon dioxide emissions. The government launched a consultation on Friday on cutting the target for new EVs to as little as 50% of all new cars in 2030, down from 80% under existing rules. The consultation will include several options, including leaving the headline target unchanged, or cutting it to 70%, 60% or 50%.

headlines.title: USS George Washington reportedly en route to relieve USS Abraham Lincoln amid concerns over conditions onboard – US politics live
headlines.description: Lincoln has been on record-breaking deployment for more than 200 days, with reports of service members attempting to jump overboard and chronic food shortages This comes after accounts about mental health crises onboard the Lincoln, including attempts from service members to jump overboard and chronic food shortages. The vessel has been on a record-breaking deployment for more than 200 days, after it was redirected to assist with the military operation in Iran.

headlinePool.title: Builders unearth €9m gold loot sealed in walls of Belgian property
headlinePool.description: Construction workers found the stash in the walls of a cellar while drilling to lay sewage pipes.

headlinePool.title: ‘Unprecedented’ rain kills five in Japan as thousands stranded at airport
headlinePool.description: Evacuation orders issued for 400,000 after flooding, landslide warnings and power outages in Chiba prefecture At least five people have died in eastern Japan after “unprecedented” heavy rain that left nearly 7,000 stranded at Tokyo’s Narita airport and forced thousands to take refuge in government buildings. The torrential rains hit Chiba prefecture, east of Tokyo, on Thursday night, triggering landslide warnings and power outages. Evacuation orders were issued for more than 400,000 people in Chiba and other areas, and about 45,000 homes lost power, as 115mm of rain fell hourly, approximately the same amount usually recorded for the whole month of August.

headlinePool.title: Two men charged with attempted murder of Sara Sharif’s father
headlinePool.description: Steven Sansom and Adam Watson accused of trying to kill Urfan Sharif, who murdered his daughter, in prison Two men have been charged over what is understood to be the attempted murder in prison of Urfan Sharif, who is serving a life sentence for murdering his 10-year-old daughter Sara. The Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) announced the charges against Steven Sansom, 47, and Adam Watson, 39, after an incident at Belmarsh prison in London.

headlinePool.title: Putin’s recruiters scramble to avoid second mass mobilisation as Ukraine losses mount
headlinePool.description: Russia is losing 30,000 casualties a month, and the country’s regions are under pressure to feed the ‘meat-grinder’. Experts say it may not be enough In kitchens and Telegram chats across Russia, the same question is being asked with growing frequency: will Vladimir Putin order another mobilisation? Nearly five years into the war, Russia is scrambling to find enough soldiers to replenish its ranks, as voluntary recruitment slows and its forces suffer heavy losses on the battlefield in Ukraine.

headlinePool.title: Memorial for second world war vandalized with bubbles and graffiti in Washington
headlinePool.description: Interior department calls incident ‘utter disgrace’ after area filled with bubbles and paint reading ‘Clean hands Dirty $’ A memorial in Washington DC for the second world war was vandalized with bubbly ⁠soap and graffiti on Thursday, prompting vows from the US government to find the perpetrator. The fountain bubbled over with suds ⁠and someone painted “Clean hands Dirty $” ⁠on one ​surface, splattering the area with red and green paint. Uniformed police and national guard troops converged on the scene, which was ⁠cordoned off with yellow crime scene tape, keeping visitors away.

headlinePool.title: Jeremy Bamber’s legal team challenge ban on his talking to the media
headlinePool.description: Lawyer says restriction comes at ‘significant moment’ in appeal process for White House Farm murder conviction The legal team of Jeremy Bamber, who has served 41 years in prison for murdering five members of his family, has challenged Wakefield prison’s decision to ban him from talking about his case to the media and long-term supporters. His lawyers have issued a claim for judicial review against the secretary of state for justice and the governor of the category A high-security prison, arguing that it is violating his right to free speech and obstructing his access to justice.

headlinePool.title: Instagram accounts fuelling Ceuta crisis with paid advice for help to cross
headlinePool.description: BBC's Top Comment podcast has found a network of Instagram profiles glamourising the swim around the Morocco-Ceuta border fence.

headlinePool.title: Almost 500 arrested on suspicion of starting wildfires in France this summer
headlinePool.description: More than 180 minors among those detained, as firefighters tackle blazes across Europe amid record-breaking heatwave Europe heatwave – latest updates Almost 500 people have been arrested on suspicion of starting wildfires in France since the start of the summer, authorities have said, as firefighters in half a dozen European countries tackle ferocious blazes amid a record-breaking heatwave. With three out of five Europeans facing temperatures of at least 30C on Friday and about 150 million enduring 35C or more, France’s interior ministry said 474 people, including 183 minors, had been detained over wildfires in the country since 1 July.

headlinePool.title: U.S. missionary who was kidnapped in Niger is released
headlinePool.description: Kevin Rideout "is in good health in the care of US officials," SIM International said in a statement, adding he would soon be reunited with his family.
